hero.headline: Spurs and Knicks meet in NBA Finals Game 1
hero.body:
The San Antonio Spurs will face the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals, with Game 1 scheduled for Wednesday in San Antonio. The matchup sets up a clash between two Eastern and Western Conference champions with contrasting roster compositions and playing styles.

The Spurs earned their Finals berth by defeating the Oklahoma City Thunder in a dramatic Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals. San Antonio won 111-103 on Saturday night, with Victor Wembanyama leading the way. The 7-foot-4 French star finished with 22 points and seven rebounds while earning series MVP honors. However, Wembanyama was quick to credit his supporting cast for the victory.

Julian Champagnie scored 20 points with six three-pointers, Dylan Harper made an impact off the bench, and Luke Kornet delivered a crucial block in the fourth quarter as Oklahoma City mounted a comeback attempt. After the game, the emotional Wembanyama reflected on reaching the Finals. "Realizing that some part of a childhood dream is going to come true," he said when asked about his tears. "We're still hungry, we want more. This feeling is so powerful, I can't explain it."

The Thunder, the defending champions, struggled without Jalen Williams due to a hamstring injury. Despite a solid performance from Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, the reigning NBA MVP who scored 35 points and had nine assists, Oklahoma City could not overcome San Antonio's balanced attack. No other Thunder player scored more than 20 points. Coach Mark Daigneault acknowledged the loss but remained confident about his team's future. "You have to grow from every experience, including the tough ones," he said. "And it's the NBA, there are tough ones."

The Knicks advanced to the Finals for the first time since 1999, seeking their first championship since 1973. This creates an interesting historical parallel, as the last time these franchises met in the Finals was in 1999, when San Antonio defeated New York 4-1.

The Finals will feature marquee matchups between Wembanyama and the Spurs against the Knicks' roster led by Jalen Brunson. Both teams have constructed their rosters through unconventional approaches that may prove difficult to replicate under current NBA conditions.

Spurs forward Champagnie expressed confidence in his team's chances heading into the series. "We never knew if we were going to get this far but when you've got the greatest player in the world things happen," he said after clinching the Western Conference championship.

The series begins Wednesday night in San Antonio as these two franchises pursue championship glory through different paths and strategies.

cards.headline: Iran strikes Kuwait airport with drones as U.S. and Iran exchange missile attacks
cards.body:
Kuwait suspended commercial flights after an Iranian drone attack damaged its international airport, injuring several people. The strike came hours after the United States and Iran traded missile and drone attacks, marking a significant escalation in regional military tensions.

The escalation began when U.S. forces fired a Hellfire missile to disable a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday. The vessel, the Botswana-flagged M/T Lexie, was heading toward Iran's Kharg Island after its crew ignored repeated warnings over 24 hours. U.S. Central Command said the aircraft targeted the tanker's engine as it passed through international waters.

In response, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps said it attacked the U.S. Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain with missiles and drones. U.S. Central Command denied that any facilities were hit. Kuwait's military reported that its air defenses were intercepting missile and drone attacks and warned the public not to approach debris or unidentified objects from the interceptions.

According to U.S. Central Command, two Iranian missiles fired at Kuwait fell short or broke apart during their flight. Three missiles targeting Bahrain were intercepted by U.S. and Bahrain air defenses. The U.S. military also defended against additional drones targeting American forces in Kuwait and said no personnel were harmed. U.S. forces shot down three Iranian attack drones that were launched toward civilian ships in regional waters.

In response, American forces conducted strikes on an Iranian military ground control station on Qeshm Island.

The latest exchange of fire highlights the breakdown in diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio claimed that a deal with Iran was within reach and that the regime had agreed to negotiate aspects of its nuclear program previously off the table. However, Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, said Iran would suspend peace talks with the U.S. in protest of Israeli operations in Lebanon.

Araghchi stated that "the ceasefire between Iran and the U.S. is unequivocally a ceasefire on all fronts, including in Lebanon. Its violation on one front is a violation of the ceasefire on all fronts."

The incident adds to growing instability in the region. This is the sixth ship that U.S. military forces have disabled since their blockade of Iran began in April. The U.S. military said it had redirected 122 vessels seeking to enter or exit Iranian ports. Kuwait's airport closure will disrupt travel throughout the Middle East and affect thousands of passengers.

cards.headline: US proposes new tariffs on 60 trading partners over forced labor
cards.teaser: The administration plans extra tariffs of 10 percent or more for most trading partners following a forced labor investigation.
cards.body:
The United States announced plans to impose additional tariffs of 10 percent or more on most of its trading partners following an investigation into forced labor practices. The proposed tariffs would affect approximately 60 economies, including Canada, Mexico, the European Union, the United Kingdom, and China.

The administration proposed tariffs of either 10 percent or 12.5 percent on goods from the affected countries. The tariff proposal specifically targets Canada, Mexico, and the EU with a 10 percent rate, according to administration officials. The move follows government probes into forced labor in international trade practices.

cards.headline: Social Security Trust Fund Faces 2032 Depletion
cards.teaser: The Social Security trust fund could run out in six years, potentially reducing monthly benefits by $500 for recipients.
cards.body:
The Social Security trust fund is projected to run out of money by 2032, leaving Congress a six-year window to address the funding crisis. According to reports, beneficiaries could see monthly benefits cut by approximately $500 if lawmakers fail to act before depletion occurs.

The timeline underscores the urgency of finding solutions to prevent insolvency. Public opinion remains divided on how best to resolve the funding shortfall, with no consensus emerging on potential fixes to the program's financial challenges.

cards.headline: Trump administration drops $1.8 billion payout fund after Republican opposition
cards.teaser: The Justice Department will not proceed with a proposed fund after facing revolt from GOP lawmakers.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has scrapped plans for a $1.8 billion compensation fund following opposition from Republican lawmakers in Congress. Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche announced that the Justice Department would not proceed with the initiative.

The fund had been framed as an anti-weaponization measure by the administration. The decision to abandon it came after significant pushback from top GOP members of Congress.

cards.headline: Canada requests 16-year extension of North American trade pact
cards.teaser: Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc formally asked US and Mexican counterparts to renew the USMCA agreement.
cards.body:
Canada's Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc has formally requested a 16-year renewal of the USMCA trade agreement in a letter to his counterparts in the United States and Mexico. The proposal seeks to extend the trade deal that governs commerce among the three North American nations.

The renewal request comes as the agreement faces its first major review period. LeBlanc's letter outlines Canada's position on maintaining the trilateral trade framework that has been central to economic relations across North America.

cards.headline: Shell operated Nigeria pipeline for years despite pollution evidence, documents reveal
cards.teaser: The oil company continued pumping through a pipeline while aware of environmental damage, according to records.
cards.body:
Documents reviewed by investigators show that Shell pumped oil through a Nigerian pipeline for years despite evidence that operations were causing pollution. The findings raise questions about the company's environmental practices in the West African nation, where oil extraction has caused widespread ecological damage.

Shell responded to the findings by saying the documents lack critical context about the complex operating environment in Nigeria at the time. While the company did not dispute the contents of the documents, it argued that conditions during the period were more complicated than the investigation suggested.

hero.headline: US and Iran exchange strikes as ceasefire talks stall
hero.body:
Tensions between the United States and Iran have escalated sharply, with both nations conducting direct military strikes that threaten ongoing diplomatic efforts to reach a ceasefire agreement.

The exchange began when US forces fired a Hellfire missile at the M/T Lexie, a Botswana-flagged tanker, in the strait of Hormuz on Tuesday. The US military said the vessel was attempting to break through an American blockade and was headed toward Iran's Kharg Island. According to US Central Command, the crew had ignored repeated warnings over a 24-hour period before the strike disabled the ship's engine. This marked the sixth vessel the US military has disabled since the blockade began in April.

Iran responded swiftly. The Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps attacked US and allied positions across the region with missiles and drones. Kuwait reported intercepting missile and drone attacks at its airport, with at least one strike injuring people and forcing the suspension of commercial flights. Sirens also sounded in Bahrain as the country's air defenses worked to repel incoming fire.

US Central Command said it successfully defended against the Iranian attacks. The military reported that two Iranian missiles fired at Kuwait "fell short or broke apart" and that three missiles targeting Bahrain were intercepted by US and Bahrain's defenses. Centcom also said it shot down three Iranian drones that were threatening civilian vessels transiting regional waters.

In addition to defending against attacks, US forces conducted strikes on an Iranian military ground control station on Qeshm Island. Iran's foreign ministry claimed the attacks targeted civilian infrastructure, though the US military characterized the strikes as defensive measures against military facilities.

The military escalation comes as ceasefire negotiations have stalled. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that a deal with Tehran was within reach and claimed Iran had agreed to discuss nuclear program aspects it had previously refused to negotiate. However, Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi sent a different message, indicating that Iran would suspend peace talks with the US to protest Israeli military operations in Lebanon. He stated that any ceasefire between Iran and the US must include all fronts, and that violations in Lebanon would constitute violations of any broader agreement.

The situation has been further complicated by ongoing Israeli military operations. Despite Trump administration claims of a ceasefire agreement in Lebanon, Israeli warplanes launched dozens of strikes across southern Lebanon on Tuesday, killing at least six civilians in one strike near Sidon.

The latest round of strikes underscores the fragile state of negotiations in the Middle East. With military operations escalating and diplomatic progress stalled, both nations appear to be moving away from negotiation toward continued military confrontation. The failure to maintain ceasefire momentum raises concerns about broader regional stability and the involvement of multiple nations across the conflict zone.

cards.headline: Iran targets Bahrain and Kuwait in expanded Gulf attacks
cards.teaser: Iranian strikes aimed at Bahrain and Kuwait were shot down or failed, the US military said.
cards.body:
Iran launched drone and missile attacks against Bahrain and Kuwait, with the U.S. military reporting that the strikes were either intercepted or failed to hit their targets. Kuwait suspended commercial flights after an Iranian drone struck its airport, injuring several people. The attacks marked an expansion of Iranian military operations to include American allies hosting U.S. military presence in the Gulf region.

The U.S. condemned what it characterized as "aggressive" strikes and launched retaliatory operations it described as self-defense measures. The exchange occurred as ceasefire negotiations between Iran and the U.S. stalled, with both sides conducting fresh military strikes in the region.

cards.headline: US proposes new tariffs on 60 trading partners over forced labor
cards.teaser: The administration plans extra tariffs of 10 percent or more for most trading partners following a forced labor investigation.
cards.body:
The United States announced plans to impose additional tariffs of 10 percent or more on most of its trading partners following an investigation into forced labor practices. The proposed tariffs would affect approximately 60 economies, including Canada, Mexico, the European Union, the United Kingdom, and China.

The administration proposed tariffs of either 10 percent or 12.5 percent on goods from the affected countries. The tariff proposal specifically targets Canada, Mexico, and the EU with a 10 percent rate, according to administration officials. The move follows government probes into forced labor in international trade practices.

cards.headline: Drone strike on bus kills seven in Russian-controlled Ukraine
cards.teaser: A bus traveling between Moscow and Simferopol was hit by a drone in Russian-occupied territory.
cards.body:
A drone attack struck a bus traveling to Simferopol in Russian-occupied Crimea, killing seven people according to Russian officials. The bus was en route along a corridor connecting Moscow to the Crimean peninsula, which Russia has controlled since 2014.

The strike is the latest in a series of escalating attacks across Ukraine. Russia has intensified military operations, launching massive aerial assaults on Ukrainian cities including Kyiv that have killed dozens of civilians in recent days.

cards.headline: Ukrainian attack sets Russian weapons plant ablaze
cards.teaser: A weapons manufacturing facility in Tambov Oblast caught fire after a Ukrainian strike.
cards.body:
Ukrainian forces struck a Russian weapons manufacturing facility in Tambov Oblast, causing a major fire. The plant produces military equipment used by Russian forces.

As St. Petersburg prepared to host an international economic forum, Ukraine launched coordinated attacks on the city, including strikes against an oil terminal. Ukrainian drones were deployed in the operation while Russian air defenses worked to intercept them.

cards.headline: British police handcuffed dying student, sparking investigation
cards.teaser: Henry Nowak was restrained by officers while dying in a case that has drawn public outrage.
cards.body:
British authorities are investigating police officers who handcuffed student Henry Nowak while he was dying. The case has generated significant public anger and has become increasingly politicized in the United Kingdom.

Nowak's death while in police custody has raised questions about law enforcement procedures and use of restraints. The investigation focuses on the actions of the officers who applied handcuffs to Nowak during his medical emergency. The case has become a focal point for broader discussions about policing practices in Britain.

cards.headline: South Korea holds local elections as test of President Lee
cards.teaser: Voters are casting ballots in elections seen as a gauge of the president's first year in office.
cards.body:
South Koreans are voting in local elections widely viewed as a measure of President Lee's performance during the first year of the administration. The elections provide the first major electoral test since Lee took office.

The results are expected to indicate public sentiment toward the president's policies and leadership. Local elections in South Korea often serve as a referendum on the national government's approval ratings and policy direction.

cards.headline: Karen Bass advances to runoff in Los Angeles mayoral primary
cards.teaser: The incumbent mayor will face a second round of voting after finishing first in the primary election.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass won Tuesday's mayoral primary but fell short of the 50% threshold needed to avoid a runoff. She will face a challenger in November's general election to decide who controls the nation's second-largest city.

Bass's opponent in the runoff will be either Spencer Pratt, a former reality TV star, or city council member Nithya Raman, as the race between those two candidates remained too close to call on election night.

cards.headline: Drone strike kills seven on bus in Russian-controlled Ukraine
cards.teaser: The attack hit a bus traveling between Moscow and Simferopol in occupied Crimea.
cards.body:
A drone attack on a bus traveling between Moscow and Simferopol killed seven people, according to Russian officials. The bus was operating on a route through Russian-controlled territory in Ukraine, with Simferopol serving as the capital of Russian-occupied Crimea.

The strike marks another instance of drone warfare in the ongoing conflict. Russia has intensified attacks across Ukraine in recent months, with aerial assaults on major cities including Kyiv causing additional casualties among civilians.

cards.headline: Scott Wiener advances in race for Nancy Pelosi's House seat
cards.teaser: The California state senator moved forward in the primary to succeed the former House Speaker.
cards.body:
State Senator Scott Wiener advanced in the primary election for the House seat previously held by Nancy Pelosi. The race to succeed Pelosi, who represented the San Francisco district for decades and served as House Speaker, drew significant attention in California politics.

Wiener, a Democrat who has served in the California State Senate, will proceed to the general election for the congressional seat. Pelosi's retirement from the seat marked the end of an era in Bay Area and national politics, making the race to replace her one of the most watched contests in the state's primary election.

cards.headline: Trump-backed Iowa congressman loses governor primary
cards.teaser: Representative Randy Feenstra was defeated in his bid for governor despite presidential endorsement.
cards.body:
Representative Randy Feenstra lost the Republican primary for Iowa governor despite receiving an endorsement from former President Donald Trump. The defeat underscores the limits of Trump's influence in GOP primary contests.

Iowa's primary results set the stage for competitive races across the state in the November midterms. Democrats view the governor's race as one of several contests where they can be competitive in the traditionally Republican state, alongside three House races and the Senate election.

hero.headline: SpaceX Plans $75 Billion IPO at $135 Per Share
hero.body:
SpaceX is moving forward with plans for a $1.75 trillion initial public offering, with the company targeting a share price of $135 according to Reuters. The offering would involve selling 555.6 million shares in what would rank among the largest IPOs in history.

The flotation marks a significant milestone for the private company founded by Elon Musk. SpaceX operates as a sprawling business encompassing the rocket launch company, Starlink satellite broadband service, the xAI artificial intelligence startup, and the social media platform X. These operations will now be subject to public market scrutiny and quarterly reporting requirements.

The financial picture reveals a company at an inflection point. SpaceX lost $4.9 billion in 2025 on revenues of $18.7 billion, though revenue grew by a third compared to 2024. Losses have accelerated in early 2026, with the company posting a $4.3 billion loss in the first quarter versus $528 million in the same period the previous year.

The company's three business segments show uneven performance. Connectivity, housing Starlink, generated the most revenue at $11.4 billion and was the only profitable segment in the first quarter of 2026. The space division, which includes rocket launches for clients like NASA, produced $4.1 billion in revenue. The AI unit contributed $3.2 billion in revenue but lost $6.4 billion last year, driven by computing expenses for datacentre operations and Musk's Grok AI tool. Total capital expenditure reached $20.7 billion, with xAI accounting for $12.7 billion.

The prospectus reveals ambitious long-term goals extending beyond traditional commercial space ventures. SpaceX is targeting space tourism, energy production and manufacturing on the Moon and Mars, and asteroid mining. While acknowledging these markets do not yet exist, the company plans to pursue orbital compute, or datacentres in space powered by solar energy, potentially launching them by 2028.

Musk's control of the company will remain virtually absolute following the IPO. The chief executive will maintain approximately 85 percent of voting power through a dual-class share structure, where his class B shares carry 10 votes each compared to one vote per share for class A stock held by other investors.

The offering presents substantial wealth accumulation potential for Musk. He has received grants of one billion class B shares contingent on achieving a permanent human colony on Mars with at least one million inhabitants and reaching a market capitalization of $7.5 trillion. An additional 302 million shares granted in March vest upon completing space-based datacentres delivering 100 terawatts of compute annually.

SpaceX's transition to public markets comes as the company demonstrates consistent technical achievements, including regular launches and progress on its Starship vehicle for deep space missions.

cards.headline: S&P 500 Closes at Record High
cards.teaser: Stock futures held steady after the S&P 500 reached another record close, driven by gains in artificial intelligence stocks.
cards.body:
The S&P 500 reached another record high, continuing its winning streak this year. The Dow Jones Industrial Average also hit a fresh record, while stock futures showed minimal movement in after-hours trading.

Artificial intelligence stocks led the market gains, as investors remained focused on companies positioned to benefit from AI development. The rally occurred despite rising oil prices driven by Middle East tensions. Analysts observed that market strength remains concentrated in technology and AI-related sectors.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Rise on Middle East Fighting
cards.teaser: Oil prices jumped as hostilities between the United States and Iran continued, though peace negotiations remain underway.
cards.body:
Oil prices climbed amid escalating Middle East hostilities between the United States and Iran. The price increases reflected investor concerns about potential supply disruptions from the conflict.

Despite active fighting, markets showed resilience. President Trump indicated diplomatic negotiations with Tehran were ongoing, which helped temper broader market anxiety. Asian markets advanced with Tokyo's Nikkei 225 index surpassing 68,000 for the first time, suggesting investors were balancing geopolitical risks against optimism over peace talks and strong corporate earnings, particularly in artificial intelligence stocks.

cards.headline: Seven States Sue Trump Administration Over Wind Farm Deal
cards.teaser: Seven states filed a lawsuit challenging the Trump administration's payment of nearly $1 billion to halt an offshore wind farm project.
cards.body:
Seven states, including New York, filed a lawsuit challenging a deal in which the Trump administration paid a French energy company approximately $1 billion to cancel offshore wind lease agreements. The states contend the administration misused federal funds to terminate renewable energy projects.

The lawsuit seeks to block the agreement and recover the funds paid to TotalEnergies. The deal represents a significant policy reversal away from offshore wind development that the states argue violated proper procedures for using federal resources.

cards.headline: CBS Fires 60 Minutes Correspondent Scott Pelley
cards.teaser: CBS News removed Scott Pelley from 60 Minutes after months of tensions between staff and the network's editor in chief.
cards.body:
CBS News fired Scott Pelley, a veteran 60 Minutes correspondent and former CBS Evening News anchor. The dismissal was part of a broader overhaul that also resulted in the firing of the show's executive producer, executive editor, and correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega.

Pelley publicly criticized the firings during a staff meeting with newly appointed executive producer Nick Bilton and CBS News managing editor Charles Forelle, directly attacking Bari Weiss, the network's editor-in-chief. Weiss's leadership has been at the center of tensions that led to the personnel changes at the flagship newsmagazine program.

cards.headline: Colorado Tightens Oversight of Uber and Lyft
cards.teaser: Colorado enacted a law increasing scrutiny of ride-hailing companies following reports of unreported sexual assault and misconduct.
cards.body:
Colorado passed legislation strengthening oversight of Uber and Lyft operations in the state. The law specifically cites a New York Times investigation that revealed Uber received reports of sexual assault or sexual misconduct far more frequently than the company had publicly disclosed.

The new requirements will impose stricter reporting and monitoring standards on ride-hailing platforms operating in Colorado. Lawmakers pointed to the gap between internal reports Uber received and what the company shared with regulators and the public as justification for the increased scrutiny.

hero.headline: Microsoft launches Scout, a wearable AI assistant for office workers
hero.body:
Microsoft introduced Scout, a wearable AI assistant designed for office workers, at its Build developer conference. The company announced the device alongside new software tools and artificial intelligence models aimed at expanding its presence in workplace technology.

Internal documents obtained by 404 Media reveal that Microsoft aims to make users addicted to the new AI assistant. The company positions Scout as an always-on personal agent that functions like an executive assistant. Microsoft described the device as inspired by OpenClaw technology and designed to integrate seamlessly into daily work routines.

The announcement comes as Microsoft works to reduce its reliance on OpenAI and lower costs for developers. The company unveiled new AI models and introduced Work IQ APIs, which allow developers to build applications that integrate with Microsoft's AI infrastructure. Microsoft also announced it is testing the wearable gadget specifically for use in office environments.

At the Build conference, Microsoft presented additional updates for Windows developers, including plans for Linux tools and an RTX Spark desktop. The company framed the announcements as part of its effort to position Windows as a trusted platform for development and to usher in a new era of AI-driven devices.

The Scout device represents Microsoft's latest push into personal AI assistants, a market where several technology companies compete to create tools that manage tasks, schedule meetings, and provide information throughout the workday. Microsoft has not disclosed pricing or a specific release date for the wearable assistant.

cards.headline: Ubisoft remaking Rayman Legends as 3D game for October release
cards.teaser: Rayman Legends Retold will launch October 1 with 3D gameplay across multiple platforms.
cards.body:
Ubisoft is bringing Rayman Legends to three dimensions with Rayman Legends Retold, launching October 1 across PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch 2, and other platforms. All versions will feature identical content. The Nintendo Switch 2 iteration will run at 60 frames per second.

The remake transforms the original side-scrolling platformer into a full 3D experience while preserving key gameplay elements from the classic. Ubisoft provided journalists with two-hour preview sessions to experience the redesigned game firsthand.

cards.headline: Sony reveals God of War spinoff starring Kratos's wife Faye
cards.teaser: Santa Monica Studio announced God of War Laufey, featuring Faye as the protagonist alongside a ribbon and a cube.
cards.body:
Sony announced God of War Laufey, a new spinoff developed by Santa Monica Studio and coming to PlayStation 5. The game stars Faye, Kratos's wife from the main God of War series, marking a departure from games centered on Kratos and his son Atreus.

The reveal came during Sony's State of Play presentation. The studio has not yet announced a release date for the title.

cards.headline: Insomniac details Wolverine game combat, X-Men cameos, and death mechanics
cards.teaser: Developers broke down new footage showing claw combat, a low-gore option, and how Logan can die in the upcoming game.
cards.body:
Insomniac Games developers discussed new footage from the Wolverine game, revealing details about claw combat mechanics and how the protagonist Logan can die during gameplay. The team also confirmed that X-Men characters will make cameo appearances in the game. Players will have the option to enable a low-gore mode.

The developers walked through combat systems that emphasize Wolverine's signature claws as the primary weapon. The team explained the balance between the character's regenerative healing abilities and gameplay challenge, detailing the specific circumstances under which Logan can be defeated. The game is in development for PlayStation 5.

cards.headline: Saber Interactive revives Stuntman franchise after 20-year gap
cards.teaser: Stuntman Hollywood was announced at Sony State of Play and will feature high-profile licensed vehicles.
cards.body:
Saber Interactive announced Stuntman Hollywood during a Sony State of Play presentation, bringing back the Stuntman franchise after nearly 20 years. The game will release soon on PlayStation 5. Game Informer reported that the title will include big-name licensed cars.

The announcement marks the return of a franchise that last saw a release two decades ago. Saber Interactive, known for publishing Warhammer 40

cards.headline: Cybersecurity firm Cyera approaches $12 billion valuation despite losses
cards.teaser: The company is close to raising $300 million at 80 times its annual recurring revenue.
cards.body:
Cyera, a cybersecurity company, is nearing completion of a $300 million funding round that would value the firm at $12 billion. Evolution Equity Partners is leading the investment round. The valuation represents 80 times the company's annual recurring revenue multiple.

The high valuation comes despite Cyera operating at a loss. The cybersecurity sector continues to attract significant investor interest as companies seek data protection solutions. Cyera has not publicly disclosed its current annual recurring revenue figures or the extent of its operating losses.

cards.headline: Bowerbirds collect bright human objects to attract mates
cards.teaser: Male birds incorporate colorful manufactured items into their courtship displays.
cards.body:
Male bowerbirds have begun using bright human-made items in their elaborate displays designed to attract females. Researchers observed the birds incorporating manufactured objects into their courtship rituals, which traditionally involve arranging natural materials.

Scientists described the behavior as a reminder of how human activity changes the natural world in unexpected ways. The birds select colorful artificial objects and integrate them into the structures they build to impress potential mates. The adaptation shows how wildlife responds to the increasing presence of human materials in natural habitats.

No other Thunder player scored more than 20 points. Coach Mark Daigneault acknowledged the loss but remained confident about his team's future. "You have to grow from every experience, including the tough ones," he said. "And it's the NBA, there are tough ones."

The Knicks advanced to the Finals for the first time since 1999, seeking their first championship since 1973. This creates an interesting historical parallel, as the last time these franchises met in the Finals was in 1999, when San Antonio defeated New York 4-1.

The Finals will feature marquee matchups between Wembanyama and the Spurs against the Knicks' roster led by Jalen Brunson. Both teams have constructed their rosters through unconventional approaches that may prove difficult to replicate under current NBA conditions.

Spurs forward Champagnie expressed confidence in his team's chances heading into the series. "We never knew if we were going to get this far but when you've got the greatest player in the world things happen," he said after clinching the Western Conference championship.

The series begins Wednesday night in San Antonio as these two franchises pursue championship glory through different paths and strategies.

cards.headline: Golden Knights defeat Hurricanes in Stanley Cup Final opener
cards.teaser: Vegas rallied from behind to win Game 1 of the Stanley Cup Final against Carolina.
cards.body:
Tomas Hertl scored the game-winning goal in the third period as the Vegas Golden Knights rallied past the Carolina Hurricanes 5-4 in Game 1 of the Stanley Cup Final in Raleigh, North Carolina.

The Hurricanes built an early two-goal lead but couldn't hold on as Vegas mounted a comeback. Shea Theodore led the Golden Knights with three points, while Brett Howden, Ivan Barbashev, and William Karlsson also scored. The victory puts Vegas three wins away from claiming their second Stanley Cup championship.

cards.headline: Red Sox pitcher Garrett Crochet sidelined with lat strain
cards.teaser: Boston's Garrett Crochet has been diagnosed with a low-grade lat strain and shut down from throwing.
cards.body:
Boston Red Sox pitcher Garrett Crochet has been diagnosed with a low-grade lat strain following an MRI. The injury represents a setback for Crochet, who has been experiencing tightness in his left lat. He has been shut down from throwing activities.

The Red Sox described the issue as a very minor setback related to the lat tightness. Crochet will be unavailable while he recovers from the strain. The team has not provided a timeline for his return to throwing or game action.

cards.headline: Aston Villa forward Kirsty Hanson set to join Tottenham
cards.teaser: The Women's Super League top scorer is leaving Aston Villa for Spurs after an impressive season.
cards.body:
Aston Villa forward Kirsty Hanson is set to join Tottenham following an impressive season in the Women's Super League. Hanson has been one of Villa's standout performers, making her an attractive prospect for the north London club.

The transfer will see Hanson move to Spurs ahead of the next campaign as she looks to continue her development at a new club.

cards.headline: Kentucky basketball lands transfer Milan Momcilovic
cards.teaser: Former Iowa State player Milan Momcilovic has committed to Kentucky in a high-profile transfer portal move.
cards.body:
Milan Momcilovic, a former Iowa State star, has transferred to Kentucky basketball. Momcilovic chose Kentucky over other programs including Louisville, Arizona, and St. John's in a competitive recruitment process. Reports indicate the transfer involved significant financial terms, with one outlet reporting a figure of six million dollars.

Momcilovic's commitment represents a major addition for Kentucky through the transfer portal. National media reactions have characterized the acquisition as bringing hope to the program. The transfer continues Kentucky's active approach to roster building through the portal system.

cards.headline: Patriots receiver A.J. Brown says knee concerns are unfounded
cards.teaser: The wide receiver addressed questions about his health following his departure from Eagles OTAs.
cards.body:
A.J. Brown stated that his knees are fine and that there is nothing to worry about regarding his health. The comments came after Brown departed from Eagles organized team activities, which drew mixed reactions from teammates and observers.

Brown also revealed he chose to wear number one with the Patriots despite receiving permission from Julian Edelman to wear number eleven. The receiver's first practice with New England has been analyzed as he transitions to his new team. His trade from Philadelphia did not include a first-round pick for 2027, which the Eagles had sought in negotiations.

cards.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy pleased with spring workout attendance
cards.teaser: The Pittsburgh coach expressed satisfaction with player participation during voluntary workouts.
cards.body:
Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said he is pleased with player turnout during spring workouts. The voluntary sessions have seen strong participation from the roster as the team prepares for mandatory minicamp this week.

Safety DeShon Elliott discussed his recovery from a season-ending injury sustained in 2025, saying he has put it behind him and is in good health now. The team's minicamp will provide additional evaluation opportunities as Pittsburgh continues its offseason program.

hero.headline: R&B Singer Peabo Bryson Dies at 75
hero.body:
Peabo Bryson, the Grammy-winning R&B singer known for his powerful tenor voice and iconic Disney ballads, has died at 75. Multiple outlets confirmed his death, with reports indicating he had previously suffered a stroke.

Bryson achieved widespread recognition for performing theme songs from two Disney animated classics. He recorded "Beauty and the Beast" with Celine Dion in 1991 and "A Whole New World" with Regina Belle for "Aladdin" in 1992. Both duets became cultural touchstones and earned him Grammy Awards, cementing his place in popular music history.

Born in South Carolina, Bryson built a successful career in R&B and soul music spanning several decades. His smooth vocal style and romantic ballads made him a staple of adult contemporary radio. Beyond his Disney work, he recorded numerous solo albums and collaborated with other major artists throughout his career.

The singer's Disney performances introduced his voice to multiple generations of listeners. "Beauty and the Beast" won the Academy Award for Best Original Song and topped the Billboard Hot 100 chart. "A Whole New World" similarly won the Oscar and became one of the best-selling singles of 1993. Both songs remain among the most recognizable movie themes in Disney's catalog.

Bryson's influence extended beyond his chart success. His vocal technique and interpretive skills influenced numerous R&B and pop singers who followed. The combination of his technical ability and emotional delivery set a standard for romantic ballads during the 1980s and 1990s. His work with Disney brought theatrical-style vocals to mainstream pop music and demonstrated how film soundtracks could launch songs to commercial success independent of the movies themselves.

cards.headline: CBS News Fires 60 Minutes Correspondent Scott Pelley
cards.teaser: CBS News terminated veteran correspondent Scott Pelley after a confrontation with the show's new executive producer.
cards.body:
CBS News fired Scott Pelley from 60 Minutes following a confrontation with new leadership at the network. The termination was part of a broader shake-up that also removed the show's executive producer, executive editor, and correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega.

During a staff meeting with newly appointed executive producer Nick Bilton and CBS News managing editor Charles Forelle, Pelley directly criticized Bari Weiss, the network's editor-in-chief, over the personnel changes. Pelley subsequently stated he no longer recognizes 60 Minutes following the Paramount Skydance takeover of CBS News, accusing executives of incompetence and unprofessionalism.

cards.headline: Karen Bass and Spencer Pratt Advance in Los Angeles Mayoral Primary
cards.teaser: Early returns show Karen Bass and Spencer Pratt leading the race for Los Angeles mayor, with Bass securing a runoff spot.
cards.body:
Karen Bass secured the top position in Tuesday's Los Angeles mayoral primary, earning a spot in November's general election runoff. However, she fell short of winning an outright majority, capturing less than 50% of the vote.

The race for the second runoff spot remains competitive between Spencer Pratt, a former reality TV star, and City Councilwoman Nithya Raman. As of Tuesday evening, the outcome between these two candidates had not yet been determined.

cards.headline: Xavier Becerra and Steve Hilton Lead California Governor Primary
cards.teaser: Xavier Becerra and Steve Hilton lead early returns in the California governor primary, with Tom Steyer trailing in third.
cards.body:
Xavier Becerra and Steve Hilton emerged as frontrunners in California's gubernatorial primary, with Democrat Becerra and Republican Hilton leading early returns. Tom Steyer trailed in third place. The race remained too close to call, with many ballots still uncounted. Two Democratic candidates—San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan and former Los Angeles Mayor Antonio Villaraigosa—conceded shortly after polls closed.

Under California's primary system, the top two finishers advance to the general election regardless of party affiliation. Becerra previously served as health secretary in the Biden administration. Officials expected the final results to take days to determine.

cards.headline: Tina Fey's Netflix Series The Four Seasons Draws Strong Reviews
cards.teaser: The Four Seasons, starring Tina Fey and Steve Carell, has become a streaming hit with its second season earning critical praise.
cards.body:
Tina Fey's Netflix series The Four Seasons has dominated streaming charts with its second season. The show stars Fey alongside Steve Carell and recently added David Tennant in a romantic cliffhanger role, according to the show's co-creator.

Critics have compared the second season favorably to Fey's earlier work on 30 Rock. The series has been described as a cozy hit, with multiple outlets highlighting its success across streaming platforms. The show filmed at various destination locations for its second season.

cards.headline: Love Island USA Returns for Eighth Season on Peacock
cards.teaser: Love Island USA premiered its eighth season with host Ariana Madix and narrator Iain Stirling, introducing five new couples.
cards.body:
Love Island USA launched its eighth season on Peacock with host Ariana Madix and narrator Iain Stirling returning to the franchise. The premiere introduced the first five couples, including marketing director Aniya Harvey from Georgia.

The show follows single contestants as they attempt to form romantic connections in a villa setting. Bombshell entries during the premiere episode created immediate tension among the established couples, according to the episode description.

cards.headline: Tom Holland Praises Zendaya as Career Lifeline
cards.teaser: Tom Holland called Zendaya a lifeline in Hollywood, saying he cannot imagine his career without her support.
cards.body:
Tom Holland described Zendaya as a lifeline in the world of Hollywood, stating he could not imagine doing his work without her. The actor made the comments while discussing their relationship and professional lives.

Holland also praised Zendaya's performances in Euphoria and The Odyssey. The two actors have worked together on multiple Spider-Man films and have been public about their relationship in recent years.

hero.headline: U.S. and Iranian forces exchange strikes as peace talks stall
hero.body:
U.S. and Iranian forces exchanged missile and drone strikes on Tuesday as diplomatic negotiations to end their conflict remained deadlocked. The military confrontation raised fresh concerns about whether peace efforts could succeed amid escalating tensions across the Middle East.

U.S. Central Command said American forces intercepted multiple Iranian ballistic missiles and drones before conducting self-defense strikes on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. military also disabled a tanker attempting to break through an American blockade of the strait. Iranian missiles fired at Kuwait fell short or broke apart during flight, while three missiles launched at Bahrain were intercepted by U.S. and Bahraini air defense forces.

The Iranian foreign ministry condemned the U.S. attacks as "an act of bad faith" and "a definitive violation of the ceasefire," according to reports. The strikes killed four Iranian soldiers. However, Iran's military announced no specific reprisals, suggesting reluctance to disrupt ongoing negotiations. Iran's parliamentary speaker and chief negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, remained in Doha to continue peace discussions mediated by Pakistan and Qatar.

The proposed ceasefire agreement would end the war but requires resolving several contentious issues. Ghalibaf focused on how more than $12 billion in frozen Iranian assets could be transferred to Iranian accounts. Reports indicate this remains the last serious dispute between Tehran and Washington. Iran also seeks sanctions relief on its oil and petrochemical exports during a 60-day period allocated for negotiating constraints on Iran's nuclear program.

A separate 30-day timeline in the agreement would allow the U.S. to lift its blockade of Iranian oil ports and Iran to allow commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, restoring maritime traffic to pre-war levels. The agreement faces pressure from hardliners on all sides, each demanding their negotiators avoid further concessions.

The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical chokepoint for global energy supplies, making any military activity in the region significant for international markets. Brent oil futures climbed 4 percent following news of the renewed fighting.

Beyond direct U.S.-Iran tensions, Israel's military operations in Lebanon complicated negotiations. Israel issued new evacuation warnings for residents of 19 villages in southern Lebanon as it expanded ground operations deeper into Lebanese territory. Lebanese health officials reported Israeli strikes killed 31 people and wounded 40 in recent hours. Iran's supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, called for unity among Muslim countries and projected confidence despite the escalating conflict.

The timing raised questions about whether negotiations could overcome mounting military pressures. Neither government indicated whether renewed diplomatic efforts were planned following Tuesday's military exchanges.

cards.headline: CBS News fires Scott Pelley after confrontation with new '60 Minutes' producer
cards.teaser: The veteran anchor was terminated after publicly criticizing new executive producer Nick Bilton and CBS News leadership during a staff meeting.
cards.body:
Scott Pelley, a veteran correspondent at '60 Minutes,' clashed with CBS News management during a staff meeting on Monday. The confrontation involved newly appointed executive producer Nick Bilton and came as the network was overhauling the show's leadership.

Pelley objected to recent decisions by CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss, criticizing the firing of the show's executive producer, executive editor, and two fellow correspondents, Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega. The heated exchange revealed deep tensions between the veteran talent and the new management team reshaping the flagship program.

cards.headline: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Haaland could become the first Native American woman elected governor in the United States if she wins in November.
cards.body:
Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary in the race to succeed Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham in New Mexico, according to Decision Desk HQ. Haaland celebrated at a historic plaza in Albuquerque's Old Town neighborhood.

If elected in November, Haaland would make history as the first Native American woman to serve as governor of any U.S. state. She previously served in President Biden's Cabinet as Interior Secretary.

cards.headline: California governor primary results show Becerra and Hilton leading
cards.teaser: Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer and Xavier Becerra compete against Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton to replace Gov. Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Results are coming in for California's gubernatorial primary election. Three candidates emerged at the top of the crowded race: Republican Steve Hilton and Democrats Xavier Becerra and Tom Steyer. With many ballots still to be counted, the contest remained too close to call on Tuesday night.

Two Democratic candidates conceded shortly after polls closed. San Jose mayor Matt Mahan and former Los Angeles mayor Antonio Villaraigosa withdrew from the race as early returns showed them trailing the frontrunners.

cards.headline: Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass advances to runoff election
cards.teaser: The first-term Democratic mayor will compete in the general election, though her opponent has yet to be determined.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass advanced to November's general election after winning Tuesday's primary with less than 50% of the vote. The incumbent Democrat will face either Republican Spencer Pratt, a former reality TV star, or city council member Nithya Raman in the runoff.

Bass came out ahead in the competitive three-way race, though the identity of her November opponent remained undetermined based on early results. The mayoral contest has drawn significant national attention.

cards.headline: Iowa sets up Sand-Lahn matchup for governor in November
cards.teaser: Democratic State Auditor Rob Sand and Republican businessman Zach Lahn won their party primaries to compete for the governorship.
cards.body:
State Auditor Rob Sand will face businessman Zach Lahn in November's gubernatorial election. Sand won the Democratic primary uncontested, while Lahn prevailed in a competitive Republican primary field.

Iowa's governor's race is among several competitive elections Democrats believe they can win in the traditionally Republican state. The November general election will determine who replaces retiring Governor Kim Reynolds.

cards.headline: Rep. Miller-Meeks and Christina Bohannan to face off again in Iowa House race
cards.teaser: The November contest will mark the third consecutive election between the two candidates in Iowa's 1st Congressional District.
cards.body:
GOP Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks and Democrat Christina Bohannan are projected to compete again in Iowa's 1st Congressional District in November, according to Decision Desk HQ. Both candidates handily defeated their primary opponents, David Pautsch and Travis Terrell.

Bohannan is a former member of the Iowa House. The November election will be the third straight contest pitting Miller-Meeks against Bohannan in the district.
